newsitem.title: UK: London gold steady at fix but tone still bearish.
newsitem.headline: London gold steady at fix but tone still bearish.

text.p: Precious metals prices were narrowly mixed in European business on Thursday after gold had its lowest fix since October 1993 on Wednesday morning.
But the tone remained bearish overall with the prospect of further central bank gold sales keeping the market cowed, traders said.
Gold was fixed at $354.00 per ounce after $354.45 previously and a London close of $353.90/$354.40. The Wednesday morning fix of $352.45 was the lowest since October 4, 1993.
"There might be a maximum of four dollars on the upside in this market. Between $356-$358 is where to sell," a dealer said.
Gold has had a mixed ride since London's Wednesday close, after which dollar strength weakened values in New York.
However, dealers said the New York price held up better than expected with February Comex gold down just $1.50 at $353.20 after striking a contract low earlier in the session.
The price began to pick up in Hong Kong, despite local investor selling in Tokyo, on a combination of late buying from Japan, physical offtake and early short covering from Europe.
"There has been some producer selling but there is no real interest to buy other than short covering. Physical interest at these levels has been nothing special," a dealer said.
Gold has been hovering over steep falls all week.
Weakness was triggered by news on Monday that the Dutch central bank had sold 300 tonnes of gold from reserves.

The news initially lifted some of the market despondency created by long-running rumours that a central bank had been selling bullion. But the fear of further central bank dishoarding quickly sent the price tumbling.
"I still think we are heading towards $340, although not necessarily in a straight line," one dealer said.
The other precious metals were very quiet as gold continued to hold centre stage in the complex.
Palladium was about $1.90 firmer at $121.00/$122.00, reflecting the continuing silence from Moscow over opening talks with Japanese importers for 1997's platinum group metal exports.

Platinum was less influenced by the Russian issue -- Japan has been taking an increasing percentage of its platinum imports from South Africa recently -- and was indicated at $359.25/$360.25, down about 65 cents on the close.
Silver howevered around unchanged and at 1055 GMT was a cent under the Wednesday close at $4.68./$4.70.
